method: Evidence is separated from interpretation. External statistics are marked observed; statements derived from the project's own canonical architecture are marked interpretation or mythological. No symbolic statement is presented as empirical proof.

facts.claim: EU general government debt was 81.7% of GDP at the end of 2025.
France general government debt was 115.6% of GDP at the end of 2025.
Belgium general government debt was 107.9% of GDP at the end of 2025.
Denmark general government debt was 27.9% of GDP at the end of 2025.
The EU single market is organized around free movement of goods, services, capital and people.
EU energy policy treats security of supply, affordability, sustainability and an integrated internal energy market as connected policy objectives.
Euro-area net saving was €902 billion in the four quarters through Q1 2026, while net non-financial investment was €629 billion.
Euro-area household debt-to-income was 81.0% in Q1 2026; non-financial-corporation consolidated debt-to-GDP was 65.6% in the same release.

In the 12 months through June 2026, euro-area residents made €352 billion of net direct investment in non-euro-area assets, while non-residents made €71 billion of net direct investment in euro-area assets.
In the 12 months through June 2026, non-residents made €624 billion of net purchases of euro-area debt securities.
At the latest ECB indicator update, euro-area GDP at market prices was €4,050.0 billion in Q1 2026 and M3 was €17,614.0 billion in July 2026.
EU R&D expenditure was estimated at €403.1 billion in 2024, equal to 2.2% of GDP; the business sector accounted for 66.5%.
Preliminary EU government budget allocations for R&D were €130.2 billion in 2025, equal to 0.69% of GDP.
Denmark's preliminary government R&D budget allocation was €627.1 per inhabitant in 2025, among the highest in the EU.
EU energy imports dependency was 57% in 2024, meaning net imports supplied nearly three-fifths of gross energy needs under Eurostat's definition.
In 2024, oil and petroleum products represented 67% of EU energy imports and natural gas 24%.
In 2025, the United States was the largest partner for EU LNG imports, while Norway was the largest partner for gaseous natural gas and petroleum oils.
EU social protection benefits expenditure reached an estimated €4,925 billion in 2024, or 27.3% of EU GDP.
Old-age benefits represented €2,044 billion, or 41.5% of EU social protection benefits in 2024; sickness and healthcare represented €1,463 billion, or 29.7%.
EU goods trade within the EU reached €4,142.9 billion in 2025, up 2.6% from 2024; extra-EU exports were €2,645.0 billion.
The 2024 FIGARO tables connect national accounts with business, trade and jobs across EU members and 18 main EU trading partners, with 64 industries and 64 products.
FIGARO-E3 extends input-output analysis with employment, energy and greenhouse-gas accounts, making production relationships analyzable alongside labour and environmental effects.

EU institutional responsibilities are distributed across the European Parliament, European Council, Council of the EU and European Commission, with the Court of Justice, ECB and Court of Auditors among complementary institutions.

The European Commission's AMECO database contains macroeconomic data for the EU, euro area, member states, candidate countries and other OECD countries and provides population, employment and fiscal series among others.
The canonical Frame explicitly separates observed, calculated, estimated, scenario, interpretation, historical, mythological and creative evidence classes and states that metaphor is not evidence.
The canonical Frame defines the vertical architecture from Source through Father, Father's House, Heaven, Throne of North, Ladder, Door, Son, Axis, Tree of Life, Plane, Roots and Potato of Life.
The Frame defines Tree of Life roots as origin-memory-potential, trunk as axis-continuity, branches as differentiation, fruit as manifestation and seed as renewal.
The Frame defines Tree of Strife as a fragmented-tree pattern in which relationships are replaced by fear, competition, extraction and conflict.
The Frame defines Red Potato through creativity, love, expansion, emergence, sprouting and forward movement.
The Frame defines Blue Potato through memory, precision, contraction, rootward movement, fear and conservation.
The canonical tree contains ten permanent levels: Source, Separation, Ladder, Door, Son, Tree of Life, Tree of Strife, Potato, World and North Programme.

The North Programme is represented in the canonical tree as a research/application layer containing the North Axis, participating geographies, European Economic Graph and domains including public finance, debt, ownership, infrastructure, energy, industry, research, labour, technology, dependencies and alliances.
The canonical tree explicitly includes Father–Son Relationship as a child of Separation, making the relationship itself a first-class record rather than merely a connection between two names.
The canonical tree explicitly includes Spirit–Matter, Heaven–Earth, Life–Death and Above–Below as polarity records under Separation.

The Ladder branch explicitly contains levels, spine, 33 Levels, cardinal directions, ascent, descent, mountain and North Gate, defining the ladder as both vertical sequence and navigable coordinate system.
The Door branch explicitly contains Narrow Gate, Vessel, Interface, Pineal Gland, Experience, Perception and Passage, making threshold, embodiment and perception distinct records.
The Son branch explicitly includes Thomas, Twin, Lion, Lion of Judah, Jesus Christ, Son of Man, Death, Crucifixion, Christmas, North Pole and transformation records.
The Tree of Life branch explicitly contains roots, trunk, axis, branches, leaves, fruit, seed, life, growth, memory, renewal, love, light and creation.
The Tree of Strife branch explicitly contains strife, swamp, mud, drain, fear, anger, exploitation, stagnation, fragmentation, false structures, loss of connection and return.

The World branch explicitly connects matter, biology, people, families, animals, places, nations, kingdoms, societies, institutions, laws, economies, technology, infrastructure, history, war, trade, money, ownership, obligations and alliances.
The North Programme's European Economic Graph is intended to connect entities and relationships rather than treat economic actors as isolated records.

One Economic Field is a framework proposition: national economies remain institutionally distinct while their production, finance, energy, labour, infrastructure and trade relationships are mapped as a connected system.
Public Finance is treated in the archive as a system of revenue, expenditure, deficit, debt, transfers and investment rather than a single debt number.
Industry is treated as a network joining productive enterprises, factories, machinery, skills, energy, materials and supply chains.
Research is treated as an innovation system connecting universities, institutes, laboratories, public programmes and private R&D rather than as a single expenditure line.
Labour is treated as a system connecting employment, skills, wages, participation, migration and institutions to productive activity.
Repair is treated as an applied process: identify broken relationships, bottlenecks and waste, then restore productive connections while preserving functioning capacity.
Britain is deliberately retained as a geographic node in the canonical tree and is not silently equated with the sovereign-state record for the United Kingdom.
